title: Ad-hoc micro-network / chat-market kill sweep
purpose: Search current Xuzhou/Jiangsu peer groups, association chats and ad-hoc micro-networks that already exchange tiny inventory, capacity, tasks or local help. Retain only if repeated transactions are current and a control-plane gap remains after alliances/platforms are considered.
scan_rule: AD-HOC GROUP EXISTS != OPEN ROOTER GAP
If a cluster already formalized chat coordination into an alliance/platform, the route is closed.
If a group intentionally only publishes information and parties immediately transact directly, introduction is highly bypassable and recurring value capture is weak.
A candidate needs unresolved live availability, acceptance, trust, settlement or replacement friction after current marketplaces are considered.

patterns_tested.pattern: small-order production alliance / peer capacity sharing
patterns_tested.named_example: 扬州毛绒玩具小单快返联盟
observed_network: Orders can come from the alliance, member firms or external customers.
Order specifications, quantity, quality, delivery, price and payment terms are standardized.
Members confirm acceptance quickly, report production schedules and publish shortage sourcing inside the alliance.
The alliance uses shared information tools, initially including WeChat/shared documents, and tracks delivery quality and capacity.
patterns_tested.missing_edge: THE CONTROL PLANE IS ALREADY BEING BUILT BY THE CLUSTER

observed_network: Chain leaders already drive digital order receipt, fulfillment and supplier collaboration.
Supply-chain resources are being integrated through existing digital systems and chain-leader governance.
City-level industry programs explicitly promote order/data collaboration across upstream/downstream firms.

patterns_tested.pattern: farm-machinery peer finding / informal operator network
observed_network: Xuzhou-based platform connects farmers and machinery operators.
Users can post farm-work demand and operators can find work.
The platform adds dispatch, agricultural inputs, parts and ecosystem services.
patterns_tested.missing_edge: FORMER INFORMAL RELATIONSHIP SEARCH IS ALREADY PRODUCTIZED

observed_network: Local groups publish real jobs and workers self-claim tasks.
Group organizers may explicitly state that parties transact directly and risk is self-borne.
incumbent_counterevidence: Large national furniture/home-service platforms already provide dispatch, guaranteed transaction flows, service tracking, warranties and enormous provider networks.
The missing trust/acceptance/settlement features of chat groups are already available in mature vertical platforms.

patterns_tested.pattern: machining order groups / external-processing chat markets
observed_network: Current machining communities receive actual customer machining inquiries and immediately publish them to paid order groups.
Capable factories contact the customer directly.
Providers pay for group/community access and exposure.
value_capture_counterevidence: The group operator explicitly positions itself as information publication rather than transaction execution and does not take transaction spread/commission.
Current machining B2B platforms already have very large registered supplier pools and tens of thousands of RFQs.
Generic small-batch machining and urgent machining routes were already closed in prior scans.
patterns_tested.rooter_risk: The strongest observed monetization is selling information/access to suppliers; buyer-provider transactions bypass the intermediary immediately.

observed_network: Merchants publish jobs, local workers contact the merchant privately, prices settle directly, and group rules attempt to suppress poaching or arbitrary price increases.
Some groups explicitly state that they only provide information and do not bear transaction risk.
patterns_tested.meaning: This proves information-only micro-networks can remain active even when formal platforms exist.
why_not_candidate: Mature guaranteed-transaction vertical platforms already offer the missing trust/service features.
Actors using the group appear to value low-cost/direct access; that behavior may reflect commission avoidance rather than willingness to pay for a heavier control plane.
Generic home services were already closed.

material_learning: Micro-networks can be real and active without creating a durable Rooter opportunity.
Mature clusters often evolve chat coordination into formal order/capacity alliances themselves.
Information-only groups can persist because participants prefer direct contact and low intermediation cost; this can be hostile to transaction-fee value capture.
The next useful question is why actors deliberately bypass formal platforms when they already exist: unresolved platform friction versus simple fee avoidance/direct relationship preference.
cross_industry_result.current_best_next_truth: Fresh Scan 018 should test platform-bypass persistence. Search current cases where actors intentionally leave or avoid a mature platform and revert to groups/direct contact. Retain only if the reason is a repeated unsolved transaction friction that Rooter can remove while still retaining value; kill if behavior is mainly commission avoidance, off-platform repeat relationships or regulatory evasion.
